chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked:

About a man who leaves his house intending to travel while he is fasting. He said: If he leaves before midday, he should break his fast and make up that day. And if he leaves after midday, he should complete his day.
ai.seo_question: What should a fasting person do if they decide to travel after the fast has begun?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the ruling for a traveler who begins fasting in their hometown without prior intention to travel, establishing a critical distinction based on the time of departure relative to midday (Zawal). It reflects the Shia juristic view that breaking the fast is required if one departs before midday, whereas leaving after midday obligates completing the fast, highlighting the interplay between intention (niyyah) and physical movement in ritual law.
